A Characterization for Tightness of the Sparse Moment-SOS Hierarchy

Jiawang Nie ,  Zheng Qu ,  Xindong Tang  and  Linghao Zhang Jiawang Nie and Linghao Zhang, Department of Mathematics, University of California San Diego, 9500 Gilman Drive, La Jolla, CA, USA, 92093. njw@math.ucsd.edu,liz010@ucsd.edu Zheng Qu, Department of Applied Mathematics, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hung Hom, Kowloon, Hong Kong. quzheng.qu@polyu.edu.hk Xindong Tang, Department of Mathematics, Hong Kong Baptist University, Kowloon Tong, Kowloon, Hong Kong. xdtang@hkbu.edu.hk
Abstract.

This paper studies the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy of relaxations for solving sparse polynomial optimization problems. We show that this sparse hierarchy is tight if and only if the objective can be written as a sum of sparse nonnegative polynomials, each of which belongs to the sum of the ideal and quadratic module generated by the corresponding sparse constraints. Based on this characterization, we give several sufficient conditions for the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy to be tight. In particular, we show that this sparse hierarchy is tight under some assumptions such as convexity, optimality conditions or finiteness of constraining sets.

Key words and phrases:
polynomial optimization, sparsity, moment, sum of squares, tight relaxation
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:
90C23, 65K10, 90C22

General polynomial optimization problems can be solved by the Moment-SOS hierarchy of semidefinite programming relaxations proposed by Lasserre [16]. It produces a sequence of lower bounds for fminsubscript𝑓f_{\min}italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_min end_POSTSUBSCRIPT, which converges to fminsubscript𝑓f_{\min}italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_min end_POSTSUBSCRIPT under the archimedeanness. Moreover, under some classical sufficient optimality conditions, the Moment-SOS hierarchy in [16] is tight, i.e., it has finite convergence [31]. Throughout the paper, the method in [16] is called the dense Moment-SOS hierarchy. We refer to the books [6, 19, 21, 32] about this topic.

The Moment-SOS hierarchy has strong performance for solving polynomial optimization. However, a concern in its computational practice is that the sizes of the resulting semidefinite programs grow quickly as the relaxation order increases. To improve computational efficiency, it is important to exploit sparsity. In some literature, the sparsity pattern in (1.1) is called correlative sparsity [17, 36], to be distinguished from term sparsity [38, 39, 40]. Some sparsity patterns can be given by arithmetic-geometric mean inequalities [11, 26, 27]. In this paper, we focus on correlative sparsity.

In this paper, we consider the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations for solving sparse polynomial optimization. We refer to (3.2)-(3.3) in Section 3 for the exact formulations of sparse Moment-SOS relaxations. The sparse relaxation has positive semidefinite (psd) matrix constraints whose sizes are much smaller than those of the dense relaxation. A convergence rate of the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is given in the recent work [15]. We refer to [9, 14, 17, 24, 33, 34, 36] for related work on the sparse polynomial optimization. Recently, sparsity has also been exploited to solve noncommutative polynomial optimization [12, 37]. Some applications can be found in [28, 41, 42, 43, 44]. Sparse Moment-SOS relaxations can be implemented in the software TSSOS [23, 38, 40].

In practice, people often observe that the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy has finite convergence, i.e., it is tight. However, there exist examples for which the dense hierarchy is tight while the sparse one is not (see [33]). To the best of the authors’ knowledge, there is very little work to characterize when the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight.

Contributions

This paper characterizes tightness of the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy, which is given in (3.2)-(3.3). Our main contributions are:

  • •

    We give a sufficient and necessary condition for the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy to be tight. More precisely, when the optimal value of (3.2) is achievable, we show that fks⁢p⁢a=fminsuperscriptsubscript𝑓𝑘𝑠𝑝𝑎subscript𝑓f_{k}^{spa}=f_{\min}italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_k end_POSTSUBSCRIPT start_POSTSUPERSCRIPT italic_s italic_p italic_a end_POSTSUPERSCRIPT = italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_min end_POSTSUBSCRIPT if and only if there exist polynomials pi∈ℝ⁢[xΔi]subscript𝑝𝑖ℝdelimited-[]subscript𝑥subscriptΔ𝑖p_{i}\in\mathbb{R}[x_{\Delta_{i}}]italic_p start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_i end_POSTSUBSCRIPT ∈ blackboard_R [ italic_x start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_Δ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_i end_POSTSUBSCRIPT end_POSTSUBSCRIPT ] such that (see Section 2 for the meaning of notation below)

    We remark that the first equation in (1.4) is equivalent to

    f−fmin=(f1+p1)+⋯+(fm+pm).𝑓subscript𝑓subscript𝑓1subscript𝑝1⋯subscript𝑓𝑚subscript𝑝𝑚f-f_{\min}\,=\,(f_{1}+p_{1})+\cdots+(f_{m}+p_{m}).italic_f - italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_min end_POSTSUBSCRIPT = ( italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT + italic_p start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT ) + ⋯ + ( italic_f start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_m end_POSTSUBSCRIPT + italic_p start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_m end_POSTSUBSCRIPT ) .
  • •

    Under certain conditions, we show that the tightness of sparse Moment-SOS relaxations can be certified when flat truncations hold for the minimizer of the sparse moment relaxation (3.3). This also gives minimizers for (1.1).

  • •

    For convex sparse polynomial optimization problems, we show that the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight under some general conditions. In particular, we show that the sparse relaxations are tight for all relaxation orders, when (1.1) is an SOS-convex optimization problem.

  • •

    Based on the characterization, we prove the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight when some classical sufficient optimality conditions hold or when each individual equality constraining variety is finite. In particular, when the RIP holds, we show that this sparse hierarchy is tight if each individual constraining variety is finite.

  • •

    Based on the characterization, we prove the Schmüdgen type sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight under some assumptions. In particular, we show that this sparse hierarchy is tight when the RIP holds and each individual constraining set is finite.

  • •

    We remark that this paper is the first work that characterizes tightness of the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy. Also, we give a sparse version of the flat truncation condition to detect tightness and to extract minimizers for (1.1). It is generally hard to check tightness of the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy [35]. There are almost no such results in the prior existing work, except for the case that moment matrices corresponding to intersections of blocks are rank one [17]. Moreover, we give several sufficient conditions for the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy to be tight. For the dense case, the analogues of these sufficient conditions are studied in [5, 18, 30, 31]. However, the new sufficient conditions given in this paper are not studied in earlier work because the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy requires additional assumptions for tightness. In Section 4, we show that these new sufficient conditions are satisfied for many cases; see, for instance, Theorems 4.2 and 4.6. We acknowledge that some of our results (e.g., Theorems 3.2, 3.5, 4.4, 4.5, 5.2) apply some techniques developed in the first author’s earlier work [29, 30, 31, 32].

This paper is organized as follows. Some basics on polynomial optimization and algebraic geometry are reviewed in Section 2. In Section 3, we give a characterization for the tightness of sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy, and we study how to certify the tightness and get minimizers. Section 4 gives sufficient conditions for the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy to be tight. The tightness of Schmüdgen type sparse Moment-SOS relaxations is investigated in Section 5. Some numerical experiments are presented in Section 6. Proofs for some theorems in earlier sections are given in Section 7. Section 8 draws conclusions and makes some discussions.

3.1. Characterization for the tightness

The proof of Theorem 5.2 is given in Subsection 7.6. The flat truncation (5.5) is sufficient for the dense Schmüdgen type moment relaxation (i.e., m=1𝑚1m=1italic_m = 1) to be tight, while this condition (5.5) alone cannot guarantee tightness for the sparse case, because it may not imply (5.7).

6. Some examples

This section provides numerical experiments for the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy of (3.2)-(3.3). For Examples 6.1-6.3, we use Yalmip [22] to implement sparse Moment-SOS relaxations, and apply Gloptipoly 3 [8] to check flat truncation conditions and extract minimizers. For sparse convex optimization problems in Examples 6.4-6.6, we apply the software TSSOS [23, 38, 40]. All semidefinite programs are solved by the software Mosek [1]. The computation is implemented in Julia 1.10.3/MATLAB 2023b, in an Apple MacBook Pro Laptop in macOS 14.2.1 with 12×\times×Apple M3 Pro CPU and RAM 18GB. For neatness, only four decimal digits are displayed for computational results.

8. Conclusions and Discussions

This paper studies the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy of relaxations (3.2)-(3.3) for solving sparse polynomial optimization problem (1.1). We show that this sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight if and only if (3.5) or (3.6) holds, i.e., the objective can be equivalently written as a sum of sparse nonnegative polynomials, each of which belongs to the sum of the ideal and quadratic module generated by the corresponding constraints. Under Assumption 4.1, we give some sufficient conditions for this sparse hierarchy to be tight: optimality conditions for (4.6) or finiteness of individual constraining sets. We also prove some conditions for Assumption 4.1 to hold. In particular, we show that the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy is tight under some convexity assumptions.

Here are some interesting questions for future work.

  • •

    When the RIP holds, if K𝐾Kitalic_K is a finite set but each KΔisubscript𝐾subscriptΔ𝑖K_{\Delta_{i}}italic_K start_POSTSUBSCRIPT roman_Δ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_i end_POSTSUBSCRIPT end_POSTSUBSCRIPT may not, is the Schmüdgen-type sparse hierarchy of (5.1)-(5.2) always tight?

  • •
